claim: On M3, the ANE kernel-DMA prefetcher throttles DRAM weight streaming to a 17-19 GB/s floor whenever the per-core kernel transfer is an exact multiple of 1 MiB.
evidence: D=2048 at 997.6/995.0/995.4 us vs D=1536 at 310.9 us; nominal 45-60 GB/s falls to 17-19 GB/s
caveat: Measured on an M3 Air; M1 and M5 Max are reported unaffected

claim: The nominal ANE DRAM weight-streaming bandwidth on M3 is 45-60 GB/s and the 1 MiB-multiple throttle pins it to 17-19 GB/s.
The per-core bytes a kernel-DMA task moves for a linear op X[1,D] x W[D,N] is (N/16) x D x 2 bytes, and the DMA notch fires when that value is an integer multiple of 1 MiB.
evidence: N=4096, D=2048: 256 kernels/core x 4 KiB/kernel = 1 MiB/core

claim: The ANE kernel DMA operates on 64-byte lines, so a 1 MiB transfer is exactly 0x4000 = 16384 lines, the period at which the bandwidth notch repeats.
evidence: 1 MiB / 64 B = 16384 lines = 0x4000 lines

claim: Bandwidth recovers fully within 256 DMA lines (16 KiB, one Apple Silicon VM page) either side of a 1 MiB-multiple notch, consistent with a page-deep prefetch window.
evidence: 64 B/line x 256 lines = 16 KiB = one 16 KiB page; the V notch recovers at x = +/-256 lines

claim: The 1 MiB DMA notch is a per-core state, not cross-core contention: latency was constant from 1 to 16 active ANE cores.
evidence: latency-vs-active-cores sweep flat for both D=2016 and D=2048

claim: Randomly scrambling the ANE weight address across the IOVA arena does not recover the 1 MiB-multiple bandwidth collapse, ruling out DRAM bank aliasing as the cause.
evidence: median 31.37 GB/s baseline vs 32.29 GB/s scrambled (about +1 GB/s)

claim: The suspected root cause of the 1 MiB notch is a 14-bit speculative-prefetch ring in the kernel DMA whose head/tail arithmetic omits an epoch bit, aliasing a full lap to empty.
evidence: 0x4000-line periodicity and a 256-line (one-page) recovery window match 14-bit line-pointer wraparound
caveat: Hypothesis from a black-box measurement; the author does not have the RTL source

claim: The software workaround for the 1 MiB DMA notch is to split any 1 MiB-multiple kernel-DMA task into sub-1 MiB chunks, such as two 512 KiB transfers.
evidence: two 0x2000-line tasks reach 45.52 GB/s vs 17.25 GB/s for one 0x4000-line task

claim: Splitting 1 MiB-multiple ANE kernel-DMA transfers into 512 KiB chunks yields a 2.6x-3.2x speedup, and the control experiment shows no speedup when splitting a transfer that was already sub-1-MiB.
Splitting the affected Llama 3.2 1B MLP projections raised ANE decode from 10.0 to 24.3 tokens/s with DRAM streaming rising from 24.7 to 60.0 GB/s.
The same DMA-chunking workaround raised Qwen3-8B ANE decode from 1.36 to 2.97 tokens/s with DRAM streaming rising from 22.4 to 48.7 GB/s.
Common LLM projection shapes hit the 1 MiB-per-core DMA notch, including Llama 3.2 1B gate/up/down 2048x8192 (k=2) and Qwen3-8B q/o 4096x4096 (k=2).
evidence: 7 of anemll's 15 models affected; k = MiB/lane per projection

claim: Llama 3.1 8B q/o projections at 4096x4096 and gate/up/down at 4096x14336 correspond to k=2 and k=7 MiB-per-lane, both landing on DMA-notched sizes.
evidence: projection table in the post

claim: The 1 MiB kernel-DMA bandwidth collapse is a performance erratum, not a correctness bug: the transfer still completes with correct data.
evidence: author states kernel DMA still completes the transfer correctly

claim: anemll reports that M1 and M5 Max ANE are not affected by the 1 MiB DMA bandwidth erratum while M3 is.
evidence: HN comment by anemll linking his own X post, 'M1 and M5MAX are OK'
caveat: Reported by a third party; no independent M1/M5 Max measurement fetched

claim: ANEProgramChainingPrepare error 15 is caused by using the wrong _ANEIOSurfaceOutputSets factory, not by a firmware limitation.
evidence: outputSetsWithBuffers: -> error 15; objectWithstatsSurRef:ioBuffer: -> SUCCESS

claim: With the correct IOSurface factory, both prepareChainingWithModel (daemon path) and doPrepareChainingWithModel (direct path) succeed on the ANE.
coreai-build compile with --preferred-compute neural-engine can print an ANECCompileOffline failure and still exit 0, writing a GPU-only .aimodelc with an empty ErrorList.
evidence: 'ANECCompileOffline() failed: OSStatus=0, aneCompileStatus=1, statusdict={ ErrorList = ( ... )'; 4/4 reproductions 2026-08-27/28
caveat: Linear blockwise-INT4 static weights; the palettized control compiled to 31 ANE regions

claim: Counting ANE region files after an AOT compile is the reliable placement check: find <bundle>.aimodelc -name '*ANE_region*' | wc -l returns 0 when the ANE compiler rejected the graph.
A 4B-class ANE bundle can static-load and then die on the first inference with NSPOSIXErrorDomain Code=4097 'connection to service named com.apple.ANECompilerService'.
evidence: 31 ANE regions, ~518 s cold load, warmup inference fails, 2026-06-27
caveat: Cause not isolated: the same log ends in a disk-full LLVM ERROR and a Code=16 'file not found'

claim: coreai-build compile can SIGSEGV inside GPU::anePreCompileBinary with no diagnostic and no .aimodelc on a static-shape LLM with linear blockwise-INT4 weights, and this crash is fixed on current builds.
evidence: exact repro re-run 2026-08-27 exits 0 3/3; palettized control compiles to 31 ANE regions
caveat: Now fails silently instead of crashing on the same configuration

claim: A graph with a degenerate all-zero constant-mask subgraph segfaults coreai-pre-compilation-rewrite, and because that pass is shared, program.optimize(), AIModel.load and coreai-build compile all crash on it.
evidence: faulthandler stack passes.py:261 apply_passes_sync <- asset.py:230 optimize
caveat: Reproduced on a swin U-Net no-shift path; workaround builds the constant mask outside forward

claim: Multi-input ANE requests on the direct MIL path cause a 0x1d error, so inputs must be packed into one spatial dimension.
caveat: Single-input constraint is a known limitation of the direct-API training code, not independently reproduced here

claim: MLModelConfiguration.computeUnits = .all is a preference, not a guarantee, and Core ML will fall back to GPU or CPU without error.
On macOS 26.3, compute_units=ALL was reported to silently route a model to the GPU instead of the ANE at approximately 0 W of ANE power.
caveat: Reported in a sweep of community negative reports, not reproduced on our hardware

claim: On a minimal ANE-shaped graph, fp16 placed 66 ANE regions while fp32 placed 0, making dtype the first placement gate.
evidence: control probe bench/probe_ane_regions.py, dtype the only variable

claim: A GPU fallback leaves no error string when the ANE compiler is not the failure path; the only reliable signal is the ANE region count or a hardware activity counter.
SpecializationOptions.default() can silently land on CPU, so using it to isolate an accelerator failure can read a fallback as a pass.
evidence: five graph variants 'proved fine' on default() all aborted under explicit gpu/neural_engine

claim: Anecdotally, Core ML can choose the GPU even when every layer is ANE-compatible, especially when the GPU is idle, and may prefer the GPU once a model exceeds some size.
caveat: Community observation, no reproducible criterion given

claim: The Energy Model ANE power channel is frozen on M4 and reads a constant (10945781) regardless of ANE load, so reporting its zero as 'ANE unused' is a fabricated negative.
evidence: constant 10945781 under idle and under a provably-ANE Core ML workload

claim: The SoC Stats ANE_*_TRIG channel is a free-running 24 MHz clock that advances elapsed x 24e6 regardless of load, so it must not be read as activity.
evidence: 5.46 s advanced 131110395 ticks with no relation to load

claim: Unprivileged IOReport counters AMC Stats ANE DCS RD bytes and ane 0 interrupt counts distinguish 'the ANE worked' from 'the ANE was idle' without root.
evidence: idle 0 B / 0 interrupts; Core ML compute_units=ALL 128-171 GB and 24538-37368 interrupts in the same window

claim: xctrace's ane-hw-intervals instrument is blind to Core AI graphs, logging 0 intervals while a Core ML control in the same session logged 1310.
There is no public runtime API to ask which processor Core ML or Core AI used for a model.
caveat: Detection is via debugger breakpoints, Instruments, or power counters instead

claim: FP16 backward matmuls on the ANE underflow, and the fix in maderix/ANE is a global loss scale of 256 x NLAYERS.
evidence: Limitations section: 'FP16 gradient underflow ... fixed with global loss scaling (256 * NLAYERS)'

claim: ANE SDPA ignores attn_mask in hardware, so causal attention must be decomposed as Q@K^T on the ANE, mask+softmax on the CPU, then scores@V on the ANE.
The ANE softmax mishandles IEEE -inf, so a causal mask must use -40000.0 rather than -inf.
evidence: causal mask shape (1, key, 1, query), masked value -40000.0

claim: The ANE appears to use fp16 for all weights and intermediates, so activations larger than about 1e2 or smaller than about 1e-4 lose precision and very small values become 0.
caveat: Community observation; the same file flags 16-bit weight storage as sometimes slower than 32-bit on the ANE

claim: A 4-bit k-means-g32 MiniCPM5-2B ANE bundle passed the 3-prompt token gate and then scored 131/200 on GSM8K versus 172/200 for the fp32 checkpoint, a 20-point task-accuracy loss.
evidence: 4-bit g32 phone 131; fp32 Mac 172; 6-bit g8 phone 173

claim: Keeping RMSNorm reductions in fp32 on an otherwise fp16/int8 ANE model is required to prevent bounding boxes collapsing and caption tails degrading because true-fp16 reductions lose too much precision.
evidence: language residency ~92% of cost, not 100%, because the reductions stay fp32

claim: A float32 embedding table forces coreai-build to emit 0 ANE regions and the whole model falls back to the GPU, so --disable-embedding-quantization-ios is not an ANE arm.
MPSGraph's fused SDPA requires a single head_dim; a model whose qk_head_dim differs from v_head_dim fails to lower with 'query and value must have matching inner dimension but have 192 and 128'.
evidence: Ling-3.0-tiny qk 192, v 128, 2026-08-21; fix pads V in KV cache and slices the output

claim: A fixed-capacity KV cache must be zero-initialised rather than NaN-initialised because 0 * NaN = NaN survives a masked SDPA in a fixed graph.
Pruned SD-2.1 attention overflows to NaN in fp16 and upcast_attention has no effect because the diffusers SDPA processor ignores it, so fp32 is the shipped precision.
evidence: fp32 matches the torch reference at cosine 1.000012

claim: int4 weights (linear or k-means) flip the next-token argmax for these LLMs, making int8 the practical exactness floor and int8 mandatory for the gate/up MLP.
FP16 softplus overflow was reported as a distinct ANE numerical failure alongside a W4+ANE segfault at coremltools 9.0.
caveat: Listed in a community negative-report sweep; no reproduced log in this corpus

claim: Using 16-bit-float weight storage in an mlmodel was observed to be slower on the ANE than 32-bit storage, though the cause was not established.
caveat: Author states he is not sure what is going on; anecdotal

claim: Direct use of _ANEClient and _ANECompiler private APIs may break with any macOS update because the APIs carry no public stability guarantee.
evidence: repository disclaimer

claim: The ane-infer project states its private-API usage breaks with macOS updates and is not production-ready.
evidence: 'Not production-ready. Private API usage means it breaks with macOS updates.'

claim: An OS build update invalidates every specialization cache, forcing ANE bundles to rebuild their programs on first load, measured at 325 s for a 2B 8-bit bundle and 795 s for a Qwen3-1.7B 6-bit bundle.
evidence: 24A435 -> 24A437 update; ~22 GB old cache became dead weight

claim: The ANE compiler leaks and allows roughly 119 compiles per process before failing, worked around in maderix/ANE with an exec() restart plus checkpoint.
evidence: Limitations: '~119 compile limit ... worked around via exec() restart with checkpoint'
caveat: Exact count is a reported figure, not a published specification

claim: On iOS the on-device compiler miscompiles dynamically-sized-KV specializations at sequence length 2048 or greater, corrupting output from the first generated token.
evidence: shipped workaround caps a pipelined turn's KV pre-grow at 1024 on iOS; coreai-kit#5

claim: Apple Watch S12 and Ultra 4 reboots were traced to an ANE timeout in panic-full logs.
caveat: Reported in a sweep of community reports; no primary log fetched or reproduced here

claim: An iOS 27 background-ANE entitlement change was reported, along with a report that the ANE is not revoked when an app backgrounds (unlike the GPU) and retains 79% throughput.
caveat: Secondary sweep report; verify on our own device before relying on it

claim: A data-indexed mutable_slice_update write SIGSEGVs the WWDC26 beta on GPU+ANE, so a shape-symint index or host cache must be used instead.

expectFrequentReshapes on a fixed-shape graph kills an AOT bundle on iOS: the runtime abandons the specialization, compiles on device, and segfaults in the MPSGraph AICode compiler with no error string.
caveat: Swift-only concern; not exposed in the Python runtime

claim: On the ANE path there is a hard weight-size wall located between about 1.70 GB of weights (runs) and 2.16 GB (loads but the first generation never returns) on one iPhone.
evidence: the 6-bit 2B is a 2.5 GB bundle that works (1.70 GB weights); 8-bit 2.16 GB never returns
caveat: Boundary is specific to this model/phone; practical rule is to stay under ~1.7 GB of weights per static bundle

claim: A 4B-class ANE bundle static-loads but the warmup inference fails (ANECompilerService Code=4097), leaving the GPU AOT bundle as the only on-device path at that size.
evidence: 31 ANE regions, about 518 s cold load, on-device runs 2026-06-27

claim: Only 10 of 652 Core AI assets in one survey compile to the ANE; the other 642 target the GPU.
caveat: Survey reported in the sweep; the counting method is not stated here

claim: A disk-full AOT compile can produce a same-size but corrupt ANE bundle that segfaults at load_function with no diagnostic while the bundle size and ANE region count look healthy.
evidence: 758 MB bundle identical in size to a good one; re-export with 35 GiB free loaded 5/5; was 0/8 with the disk-full bundle

claim: coreai-build compile exits 0 for any requested architecture, so a successful compile does not validate the architecture choice; only a device load does.
Core AI architecture names track the device identifier, not the marketing name: M4 Max is h16c and h16g raises RuntimeError there, while a base M4 is h16g.
A published Core AI bundle with a neuralEngine preference can compile to 0 ANE regions and run entirely on the GPU, which is the project's definition of silent GPU fallback.
evidence: fp32 published variant: 0 ANE regions, 0 GB ANE moved, 0 ANE interrupts, 10390 mW GPU

claim: An fp16 ANE graph carrying an fp32 softmax, a Python float scale, and a .float() pooling cast ran on the ANE but 3x slower than the GPU path until the f32-isms were removed.
evidence: warm median 13.14 ms (v0) -> 5.18 ms (v1, fp16 softmax) -> 4.00 ms (v3); GPU 10,390 -> 83 mW

claim: Fewer, larger ANE regions is better, not worse: ANE region count is a shape metric and not a quality metric.
evidence: v0 13 regions/122832 interrupts vs v3 1 region/13472 interrupts at ~88 GB ANE moved both

claim: On our sustained iPhone run the ANE decode rate fell about 31% once the device thermal state went from fair to serious, from 75.8 to roughly 52 tok/s.
evidence: 3 s 76.2 (fair) -> 119 s 55.6 (serious) -> plateau ~52 over 601 s

claim: An fp8-on-ANE conclusion can only be reached from documentation here because exporting an fp8 arm failed at the torch level with 'normal_kernel_cpu not implemented for Float8_e4m3fn'.
caveat: The fp8 unsupported conclusion rests on documentation, not on our own measurement

claim: The cause of the slow tail in the EXP-005 fp16 ANE variant is unidentified, and enginemon showing 0 B / 0 interrupts on an idle system rules out a persistent background ANE consumer.
evidence: candidates include ANE power-state transitions between dispatches or buffer recycling; needs a trace correlating slow samples with ane-hw-intervals

claim: An ANE run that produces a correct answer can still be architecturally pointlessly slow: an NLI-adapted model that makes one graph call per option stayed 2.5x slower than CPU on the ANE.
evidence: Von 246 ms ANE vs 98 ms CPU for 5 sequential calls; Laya's single-pass head was 29x faster on the ANE

claim: A stub MLIR dialect plugin clears two barriers to reading the cached mpsgraph bytecode — the dialect version entry (BytecodeDialectInterface::readVersion; the version payload is buffered separately, MLIR 22 BytecodeReader.cpp ~L2044) and dialect resources (OpAsmDialectInterface::declareResource/parseResource) — but every cached plan still stops at 'unexpected trailing bytes after Attribute entry': the private dialects (mps/mpsx/mps_spi/placement/anehlo/raster/llir/ane/aicode) custom-encode their attributes/types and the reader requires the hook to consume the entry's bytes exactly, which readString/readBlob do not match.
evidence: harness/p2b_mps_dialect_plugin.cpp built against Homebrew llvm@22 MLIR (harness/p2b_mps_dialect_build.sh); original_model_0 and specialized_model_1 both fail at the attribute entry, verbatim error in the wall file
caveat: LLVM-version-specific (MLIR 22.1.8); at least one custom-encoded dialect attribute per plan; the unblock is the dialects' writeAttribute encodings or reversing the kAttrType=2 section framing

claim: The PMP0 'DCS Floor | ANE-DCS-BW' voltage/frequency-floor residency is NOT a usable ANE-activity discriminator under enginemon sampling: in the matched AN-POS promotion matrix it read ~299M at idle (x2) versus ~204M during real ANE work, i.e. it is saturated by non-ANE DCS traffic (display/fabric) and does not track the ANE lane.
evidence: window totals idle1/idle2 299314198/299478449 vs ANE1/ANE2 204232761/204293119; GPU windows 147.8M/134.6M
caveat: one machine/OS build; contrasts with the 2026-10-05 r3 duty calibration (which read the floor as ANE-positive) — refractive to method (duty vs window-total); use SOC-NI9 ANEXL U instead

claim: The PMP0 'Fast-Die CE | ANE0' compute-utilization histogram is dead on M5 Max: it reads 0 in every enginemon --all window measured — idle, a confirmed-ANE full-region program (EXP-027 promotion matrix), a GPU window, and a Foundation-Model burst — so an ANE-utilisation number built on it (tmc/aneperf's ane_utilization_pct, LANDSCAPE-073) cannot work on this box, while SOC-NI9 ANEXL U correctly reports the same work as active.
evidence: PMP0/Fast-Die CE/{ANE0,MACC0,MACC1,PACC} all 0 across promote ane/gpu/idle and fm/idle windows; the channel is present in the subscription (not absent)
caveat: one chip/OS build 26A434; the histogram may deliver on other chips (aneperf targets M1+), and a different subscription mode was not tried

claim: Core ML's planner does not split an eligible conv graph across engines on M5 Max: MLComputePlan (compute_units=all) puts a pure 8-conv model entirely on the ANE and keeps a 6-conv stack with an inserted gather/pad/interp/maxpool op entirely on the ANE (only const->None alongside), while inserting a CPU-only op (topk) moves the WHOLE graph to CPU — so no non-nil cross-engine _ANESharedEvents can be produced by these shapes, and a live ANE-inter-engine chain needs a genuinely partitioned model (or capture of events at _ANERequest creation).
evidence: coremltools 9 MLComputePlan per-op device histograms over 7 candidate graphs (harness/coreml_plan.py, coreml_explore_ops.py); results/coreml_placement.txt
caveat: one machine/OS build; the search covered conv stacks with 6 inserted ops only, not every op family; Apple system models do partition but are not runnable here with known inputs

claim: Practical Core ML placement rules (measured, M5 Max / macOS 27): (1) to get work onto the ANE keep the DATA PATH fp16 - an op that must carry int32/bool data cannot run there and is placed on CPU, so integer index/mask plumbing (cast->int32, less->bool, expand_dims) splits an otherwise-ANE model; (2) PER-OP SIZE IS NOT A PREDICTOR - placement is decided for the graph as a whole, so READ THE PLAN (MLComputePlan, or harness/plan_devicesupport.m in EXP-025) instead of guessing from layer sizes; (3) the popular '~150 MFLOPs per conv' rule of thumb is only a ~+/-10% correlate for 3x3 convs, measured on single-op/tiny graphs (1x1 convs cross over lower, ~1.44-1.46e8 FLOPs; larger kernels higher); (4) computeUnits CAPS the candidate set, so 'all' can move an entire model to the GPU (measured: a 1385-op speech encoder gave 1381 ANE + 4 CPU under cpuAndNeuralEngine and 1385 GPU under all).
evidence: API-147/156/157/158/159/160, all measured on this box; per-op plan reads in the referenced results file
caveat: one machine/OS build; the graph-level aggregate rule itself is still unidentified, so (2) is a procedure rather than a formula

claim: Practical 'can this workload use the M5 GPU Neural Accelerators?' gate (documented surface, to be exercised by EXP-029): the tensor path needs Metal language 4.0 + Apple9 (M3+), M/N/K all multiples of 8 and >=8, enough tile occupancy ((M/128)(N/128)*batch>=128 for the 128-tile, or (M/64)(N/64)*batch>=16 for the 64-tile), and it prefers fp16/bf16 or fp32-via-tf32; naive MTLTensor/legacy-pipeline dispatch and row-major extent order silently produce zeros or write only tile (0,0). Practical expectation from third-party envelopes: NAX is a PREFILL/large-M lane (it wins from M~400 upward) and decode shapes (M=1) belong on the shader GEMV path; on this box the single-tile eval was dispatch-bound at 239.8 us, so small shapes gain nothing from the tensor units. TOPOLOGY (owner-flagged, must not be fumbled): NAX are INSIDE the GPU - 1 GPU core = 1 NAX (measured 40 GPU cores here => 40 NAX units), so NAX and the shader/SIMT path are two datapaths in the same core sharing one register/power/dispatch budget; 'NAX vs SIMT' is therefore intra-engine, not a lane choice, and NAX activity must never be read from ANE lenses (ANEXL U / ANE UP stay 0 for tensor work).
evidence: MetalHLO gating rules (API-162), Tungsten envelope (API-163), per-core topology (API-164), our single-tile eval (EXP-027); silent-zero causes from knowledge/ane/10 Q5
caveat: the gate and the M~400 crossover are documented/third-party, not yet measured on this box; EXP-029 tests them; EXP-029 energy arms are gated on a user quiet window

claim: Measurement windows MUST be gated on machine state: GPU idle power on this box is not constant - 29 consecutive 1 s samples in one 30 s observation gave min 25.1 / median 26.9 / max 104.3 mW (4.2x spread), and three adjacent 5 s windows with an IDENTICAL process set read 118.96 / 85.19 / 119.84 mW - so oMLX presence was NOT the variable and all three of those windows would have been invalid measurement windows. The idle band is ~25-27 mW; excursions to 56-104 mW occur inside the same 30 s. Therefore every energy/joule number needs the idle band verified before AND after, and windows with excursions discarded. Tools: results/EXP-029-nax-crosslane/harness/quiet_probe.sh (process/daemon/thermal/power/display snapshot + canary + engine baseline) and harness/canary.c (fixed CPU+memory work; MUST be built -O0 - at -O2 the loops are deleted as dead code and it reports 0.0000 s and inf GB/s, which is how the first canary version was caught). Watchlist finding during the survey: 18-20 Apple background suspects were up (mediaanalysisd/photoanalysisd/photolibraryd, cloudd x2/bird/backupd, nine mds_stores + corespotlightd, corespeechd/assistantd/modelcatalogd, aned/ANECompilerService) with one VTEncoderXPCService instance at 11.9% CPU, while the ANE itself was idle (floor duty 0.0%).
evidence: three quiet_probe.sh snapshots (results/quiet-20261010T1450*.txt) + a 30 s 1 Hz enginemon capture (results/quiet-power-20261010T1452Z.jsonl.gz, per-second series in QUIET-STATE.md)
caveat: one machine/OS build/session - the 25-27 mW band is this box today, the protocol is the deliverable; spike sources are not yet attributed per process (power was captured, not per-process GPU time)

claim: Two hazards found while arming the EXP-029 gate, both capable of corrupting measurements WITHOUT an error. (1) LOCALE: this box runs LANG=fr_FR.UTF-8 and Apple CLIs emit comma decimals there (ps gave '9,1', sysctl '3072,00M'); the first power_correlate.sh run died on float('9,1'), and bench/_power.py - the single source of truth for every power A/B - matched only '[\d.]+', so a localized '1234,56 mW' FAILED to match and the sample was DROPPED SILENTLY (fewer samples, no error). Fix: _power.py now accepts both separators (self-tested: '1234,56 mW' -> 1234.56; '1,234.56 mW' -> 1234.56) and every harness exports LC_ALL=C. (2) SCREEN SHARE is the dominant confound, not Apple's ML daemons: with the owner connected over Screen Share the 1 Hz GPU idle median is 85.0 mW (43 samples, min 32.6 / max 166.9), whereas the same session minutes earlier measured 26.9 mW median - roughly a 3x higher idle floor - and the worst second was attributed to avconferenced 13.3% + WindowServer 13.2% + VTEncoderXPCService 8.1%, i.e. the screen-capture/encode path. Consequence: energy arms should be run SSH-only/headless (expected floor ~27 mW), or the window must be gated on the screen-share band (~85 mW) explicitly.
evidence: float('9,1') ValueError in the first power_correlate.sh run; locale output showing LANG=fr_FR.UTF-8; _power.py self-test with comma decimals; results/power-corr-20261010T145954Z-screen-share.tsv (43 x 1 s GPU mW + per-process CPU) vs the 26.9 mW median in quiet-power-20261010T1452Z.jsonl.gz
caveat: PART (2) IS SUPERSEDED BY GOTCHAS-079: the owner was screen-sharing THROUGHOUT, so 'share vs no-share' was the wrong variable - the two medians are two REGIMES within one continuous sharing session, and display/compositor traffic is identical between them while AGX engine activity triples. Part (1), the locale hazard, stands. Claim text left as originally emitted (append-only spine has no in-place correction path); see GOTCHAS-079.

claim: HEADLESS BASELINE (SSH-only, no Screen Share) on this Studio: with the virtual screen-share display gone (system_profiler reports NO displays at all) and WindowServer absent, the GPU energy counter shows ZERO delta in 22 of 28 seconds (30 s capture) and 53 of 56 seconds (60 s capture); when it does move it is 1.3-3.0 mW, so the headless GPU idle floor is effectively 0-3 mW against 26.9 mW (regime A) and 82.7-85.0 mW (regime B) measured while Screen Sharing. AGX RD events/s fall from 114.6 (sharing) to 23.5 (headless). Screen Sharing therefore costs roughly 25-85 mW of continuous idle GPU power on a box whose headless floor is near zero. MANDATE: energy/joule arms run SSH-only; and note enginemon JSON omits zero-delta channels (enginemon.c:337), so a channel absent from a sample means delta 0 - never compute a rate as a median over present samples, use sum(delta)/sum(dt).
evidence: two SSH-only enginemon captures (30 s: 6/28 samples non-zero; 60 s: 3/56 non-zero; 1.3-3.0 mW when non-zero) vs the saved Screen-Share captures; system_profiler showing no displays; enginemon.c:337 for the zero-delta skip
caveat: one machine/session; the exact non-zero values are few samples, so the floor is best stated as 0-3 mW; the 24 MHz free-running DISP family is covered by GOTCHAS-082

claim: CORRECTION to GOTCHAS-078 part (2), plus a tooling rule. (a) The variable is NOT screen sharing: the owner drives this Studio over Screen Share THROUGHOUT (owner-confirmed), and two 1 Hz captures ~7 minutes apart, BOTH under Screen Share, gave GPU medians 26.9 mW (n=29, min 25.1 / max 104.3) and 82.7-85.0 mW (n=29/43, min 32.6 / max 166.9) - a 3.1x REGIME difference inside one continuous sharing session. A channel-level diff of those captures localizes it: display/compositor traffic is IDENTICAL (DISP* and DISPEXT0-3 RT RW ~2.4001e7 vs ~2.3997e7 per s; UT_EXT_THROTTLE_MGPU ~2.4004e7 vs ~2.3990e7; <0.1%) while AGX engine activity TRIPLES (AGX RD/WR events 114.6 -> 303.0 per s; AGX.Count_UT_Engagement 127.1 -> 316.2). So the high regime is genuine GPU engine WORK, not display pinning and not the ML daemons; WHICH task submits it is still unidentified - CPU hints (avconferenced 13.3% / WindowServer 13.2% / VTEncoderXPCService 8.1% in the worst second) do not prove GPU submission, and task-level attribution needs `sudo powermetrics --show-process-gpu` (user one-shot per repo policy). Protocol consequence: gate each window on ITS OWN observed band and never compare numbers taken in different regimes; a true headless floor remains unverified and needs an SSH-only session. (b) TOOLING RULE: the OpenClaims spine is append-only and `openclaims_append.py` skips already-emitted claims, so editing a record's claim text does NOT update its emitted event and a newly-set `contested` flag on an already-emitted record emits nothing. Corrections to an emitted claim must therefore be: leave the claim text as emitted, append the correction to its caveat, and file the correction as a NEW record (the API-151 -> API-153 precedent). CAVEAT: the DISPLAY-CONTROL EVIDENCE cited here is INVALID - DISP/DISPEXT channels are free-running ~24 MHz counters (see GOTCHAS-082); only the AGX evidence in this record stands.
